scope: Repair diff 5c44c4a..d968ed3 plus the standing round-1 findings. R2 and R3 confirmed closed by the reviewer; R1's fix is superseded by R9. No fresh full-diff sweep.

findings.claim: check_deep_link's new `order` list asserts textual file position, not the execution dependency it claims, so it is green on a relocation that leaves the deep link permanently dead and red on a semantics-preserving one.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1814-1821 compares `flat.find()` offsets over four pins, two of which (`if(!want || ![...$("#fx").options]...) return;` and `if(q.get("run") === "1") $("#go-fx").click();`) live inside the *body* of `function deepLink(){...}` (index.html:406-412) whose position is irrelevant to when it runs. False green: move the call site into the catch arm — `}catch(e){ $("#sha").textContent = "meta unavailable"; deepLink(); }` at index.html:393-394 — and the deep link runs ONLY when /api/meta fails, i.e. never on the happy path; `?fixture=aapl-2025&run=1` renders nothing, the same user-visible symptom as round 1's R1, and run_case returns passed=True with invariant 63/63 = 1.000 (measured). False red: hoist the whole `function deepLink(){...}` declaration above `async function boot(){` — behaviour identical (declarations hoist) — and the case fails with `out of order: 'if(!want || ![...$("#fx").options].some(o => o.value === want)) return;' (@15053) runs before 'deepLink();' (@15416)` (measured). The quoted diagnostic, the docstring at :1789-1801 ("a pin that moves ahead of its predecessor is red wherever it moved to") and the case note in evals/adversarial/ui-deep-link.json all state a guarantee only the first of the three pairs actually provides.
findings.repro: rsync the tree to a scratch dir; (a) move `deepLink();` from boot()'s tail into the catch arm, then `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant` -> [PASS] ui-deep-link, 63/63 = 1.000. (b) cut the `function deepLink(){...}` block and paste it immediately above `async function boot(){`, same command -> [FAIL] ui-deep-link.
findings.acceptance: Either the chain is pinned as containment rather than position (e.g. the call site pin is the whole `}catch(e){...}\n  deepLink();` span, so moving it out of boot()'s straight-line tail is a missing pin), or `order` is reduced to the one pair that is a real file-order dependency (options assignment -> call site) and the docstring/case note stop claiming the guard and run positions are asserted dependencies. Mutation (a) goes red; mutation (b) stays green.

findings.claim: The rewritten ui-deep-link case note quotes a `verbatim` red output whose offsets the check cannot produce, so the note's red-first evidence is fabricated.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/ui-deep-link.json triage.note ends: "that mutation is red at `out of order: 'deepLink();' (@11395) runs before '$(\"#fx\").innerHTML = m.fixtures.map(f => `<option>${esc(f)}</option>`).join(\"\");' (@11405)`". Running the reviewer's own mutation produces @14984 / @15084 — which is exactly what tasks/reviews/pr55-r1-resolution.json R1 `red_output_verbatim` records, so the resolution artifact and the case note disagree. The quoted 10-character gap is arithmetically impossible for any placement of the call site: `_squash('deepLink();')` is 11 characters, so the earliest the next pin can start is prev+11. Same note also still says "all six pinned expressions missing, six failures" while `input.wire` is now seven pins.
findings.repro: In a scratch copy move `deepLink();` to the first line of `boot()`, then `python3 -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.repo_hygiene.eval_adapter import run_case;print(run_case(json.load(open('evals/adversarial/ui-deep-link.json')))['failures'])"` -> offsets 14984/15084, not 11395/11405.
findings.acceptance: The note quotes the offsets the check actually emits (or drops the offsets and quotes only the stable prose of the message), and the pin count in the historical red-first sentence matches the current `wire` length.

findings.claim: `_named`'s IDREF resolution answers "does an element with that id exist" rather than "does the name compute non-empty", so a labelledby pointing at an element with no accessible text still reads as named — the same defect class R2 was raised for.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1649 `all(re.search(r'\bid="' + re.escape(t) + r'"', live) ...)`. Concrete input: `<div id="banner" class="s-idle" role="status" aria-labelledby="up">` — `id="up"` is the `<input type="file">` at index.html:303, whose accname computes to the empty string, so `get_by_role('status', name=...)` still matches nothing; measured `run_case(...)` passed=True, failures=[]. R2's stated acceptance ("resolves every token against an id present in the same live file") is met, so R2 is closed; the docstring's ceiling at :1638-1643 says the limit is "what does it say", which under-describes this — the limit is also "is it named at all".
findings.repro: In a scratch copy `sed -i '' 's/role="status" aria-label="doc_status"/role="status" aria-labelledby="up"/' src/sec10k/web/static/index.html && python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant` -> [PASS] ui-banner-status-role, 63/63 = 1.000.
findings.acceptance: Either the docstring ceiling names this case explicitly (a resolving reference to a text-less element is still accepted), or the browser walk asserts the banner's computed name non-empty via `get_by_role('status', name=...)` so the static check is not the only thing standing behind the claim.
